judge-easy-retry-budget.brief: Problem: a producer agent's structured payload can fail engine validation. Choose how rejected payloads are retried. The existing system has ONE bounded request-slot budget: semantic attempts 1 and 2.

candidates.design: Emission and extraction rejections both consume the existing request-slot budget: a semantic rejection at attempt 1 permits one fresh engine-issued attempt 2; rejection at attempt 2 is terminal. Diagnostic causes are recorded separately but no second counter exists.

Reuse the shared budget (attempts 1 and 2) exactly, and additionally journal a typed cause per rejection (engine-only refusal, extraction failure, duplicate call) so operators can see why attempt 2 was spent.

Inside the same spawn, feed every validation error back to the model and re-prompt until the arguments validate; only then accept the payload. No attempt limit is needed because the model always converges eventually.

judge-easy-cache-invalidation.brief: Problem: route qualification results are expensive to obtain. Choose how they are cached between runs.

candidates.design: Key every cached qualification by (provider, served model id, Pi version, frozen schema digest). Any change to one of them is a cache miss and requires requalification.
Key cached qualifications by provider name only and keep them forever, so a qualified provider never has to be probed again even after model or schema upgrades.
Key by (provider, served model id, Pi version, schema digest) and additionally expire entries after 30 days to force periodic re-probing.

judge-hard-readiness-barrier.brief: Problem: an emission-enabled Pi child must not send any model request until its emission tool is registered, active and bound to the issued request. In Pi, exceptions thrown from a before_agent_start handler are caught and the agent continues; an awaited (pending) handler does hold the agent.

candidates.design: Start the child in RPC mode without a prompt, invoke a readiness extension command (no model request), compare the bound readiness payload against the issued binding, bind the exact route, and only then deliver the task prompt. An awaited before_agent_start hold is kept as defense in depth.

Start the child in print mode with the prompt supplied. In before_agent_start, check that the emission tool is registered and throw an Error if it is not; the throw stops the agent before any model request.

Start the child in RPC mode without a prompt; the child awaits a held before_agent_start promise that is released only after its readiness command reports the registered, active tool; the launcher compares the readiness payload before delivering the prompt.

judge-hard-duplicate-identity.brief: Problem: a transcript may contain the same emission tool call more than once (transport replay) and may also contain two distinct calls (the model called twice). Exact replays must be idempotent; two distinct calls are ambiguity and must be rejected.

candidates.design: Group frames by tool-call id. Frames with the same id and identical request/kind/version/arguments are one call; same id with any differing field is contradictory and refused; two or more distinct ids are a duplicate-call rejection.

Deduplicate frames by their argument bytes: identical arguments are the same call regardless of tool-call id, and different arguments are distinct calls. This collapses replays without tracking identities.
Group frames by tool-call id and compare an argument digest within a group; refuse contradictory groups; count distinct ids for the duplicate rule, journaling each call id with its digest.

finding.claim: sumLineTotals skips the last line item, so every order total is understated by its final line.
The content-addressed revision depends on the host locale: entries are ordered with localeCompare before hashing, so two hosts can compute different revisions for identical bytes.
displayName dereferences user.name without a null check and crashes when the user is missing.
writeState races with concurrent readers: a reader can observe a half-written state file.
